title: Lovász LLL OQ-02: Algebraic Tightness of the Threshold T(d)

problemStatement.formal: Complete 2 sorries in LovaszLocalLemmaOQ02.lean: prove lllThreshold_is_maximum (T(d) maximizes p*(1-p)^d) and lllThreshold_strict_maximum (the maximum is strict) using Real AM-GM inequality
problemStatement.plain: The Lovász Local Lemma threshold T(d) = d^d/(d+1)^(d+1) is the unique maximum of p*(1-p)^d over [0,1]. The file has 2 sorry-holes: proving T(d) achieves this maximum, and proving the maximum is strict. Both require casting ℚ-arithmetic to ℝ and applying AM-GM.
whyMatters: Closes the two remaining sorries in LovaszLocalLemmaOQ02.lean (badge: wip)
Establishes algebraic tightness of the LLL threshold — proving the bound is exact

proven: lllThreshold definition: T(d) = d^d/(d+1)^(d+1) in ℚ (exact arithmetic)
LLL statement: if each event has prob ≤ p and ≤ d dependencies, and p*(1-p)^d ≤ T(d), then Pr(none happen) > 0
lllThreshold_is_maximum for small d by norm_num
open: lllThreshold_is_maximum: ∀ d : ℕ, ∀ p : ℝ, 0 ≤ p → p ≤ 1 → p * (1-p)^d ≤ T(d)
lllThreshold_strict_maximum: strict inequality unless p = T(d)
